items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: I hired Jimmy Lunceford. He worked with me for about 6 months and this was while we were in Memphis.

ctx.x: paid $2, so John, when he left Memphis they were making over $20-25 and the leader $30, because I remember once - they were very, very prejudiced in Memphis - he had such a terrific band and Jimmy Lunceford was teaching at a high school there. He and Jimmy Lunceford were very good friends (John Williams and Jimmy Lunceford). So everything that John did Jimmy would try to do something better. So he said to John, "I'm going to get a band better than that combo you have." Jimmy got himself a girl piano player and he…

So I worked there for a while. Being in the North so long I was pretty mean to get along with because I wasn't used to what was happening. Before John got his combo I got a little job out on the outskirts of Memphis and these people were ringing a bell and saying, "I want this," and telling me, "You're from the North and if you don't do what we want you to do... yeah, we'll lynch you" and this guy took me home every night, he was talking all this talk and I waited till I got in front of the house and started…
